items.title: Vince DiMartino interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, January 8, 2025
items.q: if I could play like Bunny Berigan, I could play “I Can’t Get Started,”

ctx.x: Most of them are — some of them are funny you know. Like one of them was the most depressing job for me personally okay? I get called, once again somebody was sick. It was in Rochester when I was a student. Somebody is sick and this guy calls up and says, “Can you come and play over at the 50 Acres” which was the big barn-like place you know what I mean? And they had weddings and different kinds of things, just like the first job I ever played. And so I showed up and the guy that was running the job, he was about…

the ones that I did know I could really play. And then of course I could play solos when he wanted me to play a solo, but I couldn’t play the melody ever. I’d say just — but you know I’d listen and then I sort of sometimes I could play like a part of the melody because I figured it out just like I did the first job. I used the same technique. And then Joe Benedetto, he was sitting right next to me. The saxophone player? He says he knew what was going on and he said to me, “Vince, I have only known two or three…

was this thing called “Portrait of George.” And I didn’t record it. The guy that did record it was one of the greatest trumpet players I ever heard in my life and he lived only in Cincinnati, never left there. And he died young. Somebody shot him in a bar. But this guy was the most amazing player I ever heard. So I was channeling my Frank Brown you know but I said well I’m pretty nervous about this. And the first thing that happens in this piece, “Portrait of George,” it’s George Gershwin, three tunes. And it…
